item.title: Mexico Declares War on Stinky Seaweed
item.description: A changing climate is helping to fuel the growth of a gigantic blob of foul-smelling seaweed that has washed up in some coastal communities. Mexico is fighting back.
item.dc:creator: Claire Brown
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:description: Members of the Mexican Navy removed sargassum from the shore at Puerto Morelos, on the Caribbean coast, last week.

item.title: Phoenix Species Project Announces Funds for Imperiled Wildlife
item.description: A new fund called the Phoenix Species Project will provide $200 million to help pull imperiled wildlife back from the brink of extinction.
item.dc:creator: Catrin Einhorn
item.media:description: Some of the imperiled animals included in the Phoenix Species Project.

item.title: Trump Administration Is Undoing Plans to Boost Workplace Heat Protections
item.description: The Biden administration took steps to shield workers from extreme temperatures. The Trump administration is taking a gentler approach with employers.
item.dc:creator: Scott Dance
item.category: American Federation of Labor-Congress of Industrial Organizations
item.media:description: A delivery in Wilmington, N.C., this month. Heat is linked to hundreds of workplace deaths each year, but labor groups say the true toll is unknown because heat-related illnesses are not properly tracked or reported.

item.title: U.S. Raises Threat of Steep Water Cuts in Lower Colorado River Basin
item.description: A federal plan would impose drastic water cuts on Arizona, California and Nevada in dry years over the next decade. A legal battle could follow.
item.dc:creator: Scott Dance
item.media:description: Water from the Colorado River flowing through an irrigation canal in Arizona earlier this month.

item.title: Iran War Drives Oil Profits to Highest Levels in Years
item.description: The world’s biggest oil companies are benefiting from the high commodity prices that have been a drag on the rest of the economy.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca F. Elliott
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:credit: Meridith Kohut for The New York Times
item.media:description: An Exxon Mobil refinery in Baytown, Texas. The war with Iran has been a boon for many oil producers.

item.title: What You Need to Know About Installing Plug-In Solar Panels
item.description: You can now buy panels that plug into electrical outlets, but there are some important safety issues to consider when picking and installing a system.
item.dc:creator: Ivan Penn and Claire Brown
item.media:credit: Patrick Junker for The New York Times
item.media:description: Plug-in solar panels are as large as windows, and in Germany they are often installed on balconies.

item.title: Plug-In Solar Panels Are Starting to Sprout in U.S. Backyards
item.description: Ten U.S. states have legalized systems that can be plugged into standard wall outlets. The technology typically does not require permits or electricians.
item.dc:creator: Ivan Penn and Claire Brown
item.media:credit: Poppy Lynch for The New York Times
item.media:description: Alex Ottoboni with his balcony solar panel at his condo in the San Francisco Bay Area

item.title: A City With a Plan
item.description: Cincinnati wants to take in people fleeing climate disasters. Plus, the latest on fires in Europe.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Nazaryan
item.media:description: Cincinnati has come up with a Climate Migration Readiness Plan in hopes that newcomers can help revitalize the area.

item.title: Bipartisan Anger Grows at Pentagon’s Delayed ‘Forever Chemicals’ Cleanups
item.description: Hundreds of bases are contaminated with PFAS, which are linked to low birth weight and other risks. Politicians from both parties are demanding explanations.
item.dc:creator: Hiroko Tabuchi
item.category: United States Defense and Military Forces
item.media:credit: Nina Riggio for The New York Times
item.media:description: A burned airplane fuselage used in firefighting exercises at Cannon Air Force Base in New Mexico, a PFAS-contaminated site.

item.title: How Climate Change and Tariffs Help China Raise More Cattle
item.description: As increased rain makes grasslands and cornfields possible in areas that once were deserts, the world’s largest beef importer is becoming more self-reliant by expanding domestic herds.
item.dc:creator: Keith Bradsher
item.media:credit: Gilles Sabrié for The New York Times
item.media:description: A herder taking her cows to graze in mountain pastures in northern China’s Hebei Province.

item.title: Trump Administration Is Repurposing Federal Land for A.I. Data Centers
item.description: In the latest example, the Energy Department will convert a shuttered Cold War-era uranium enrichment facility into a data center campus and gas plants.
item.dc:creator: Brad Plumer
item.media:description: President Trump and Energy Secretary Chris Wright during a White House event last week in which 200 companies vowed to prevent A.I. data centers from driving up power costs.

item.title: In Ohio, Toxic Wastewater Is Bubbling Up Out of the Ground
item.description: The state is a major importer of fracking wastewater, which gets pumped underground but doesn’t always stay there. The city of Marietta is fighting back.
item.dc:creator: Quinn Glabicki and Maddie McGarvey
item.media:credit: Maddie McGarvey for The New York Times
item.media:description: The wastewater, which can be radioactive, has risen to the surface through older oil and gas wells near Marietta, Ohio, such as this one.

item.title: Fossil Fuel Executives Cash In
item.description: Insiders at leading oil and gas companies have made millions from stocks since the Iran war began.
item.dc:creator: Claire Brown
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:description: Executives at Cheniere Energy, ConocoPhillips and other companies have sold almost $400 million in fossil fuel stocks in recent months, according to a new analysis.

item.title: The Iran War Just Put Another Key Oil Route at Risk
item.description: Attacks in the Strait of Hormuz during the Iran war have led Saudi Arabia to rely on an alternative route for exporting oil. Our reporter Rebecca F. Elliott explains how that route is now threatened by the Houthis, a Yemeni militia supported by Iran.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca F. Elliott, Paul Abowd, Nikolay Nikolov, Nour Idriss, Stephanie Swart, Rafaela Balster, Lauren Pruitt, Alexandra Ostasiewicz, Samuel Granados and Leanne Abraham

item.title: Why Restarting a Nuclear Power Plant Can Be Much Harder Than Expected
item.description: The first U.S. attempt at reopening a shuttered reactor has been held back by run-down equipment and a lack of planning.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca F. Elliott and Jamie Kelter Davis
item.media:description: Palisades opened in 1971 and was part of an early wave of reactors built in the United States.

item.title: Tankers Sail Through Red Sea Despite Houthi Blockade
item.description: Dozens of ships continued to traverse the Red Sea this week, but with scattered disruption, uncertainty about the passage grows by the hour.
item.dc:creator: Leanne Abraham and Jenny Gross
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)

item.title: Nuclear Energy Revival Puts Westinghouse in Prime Position
item.description: The company, which filed for bankruptcy protection in 2017, stands to benefit from growing support for nuclear power and President Trump’s deal with Saudi Arabia.
item.dc:creator: Ivan Penn
item.media:description: Cooling towers at the nuclear reactor facility at the Alvin W. Vogtle Electric Generating Plant in Waynesboro, Ga.

item.title: See How Houthis Put the Red Sea at Risk as an Alternative Oil Route
item.description: Saudi Arabia has diverted huge amounts of oil to the Red Sea since the Iran war began, but now the Iranian-backed Houthi militants say that they intend to block that route.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca F. Elliott, Lazaro Gamio and Samuel Granados
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)

item.title: What the Cyclospora Outbreak Reveals
item.description: Warming is expected to fuel the spread of food-borne pathogens. We might not be prepared.
item.dc:creator: Claire Brown
item.media:description: A microscopic view of cyclospora parasite eggs, stained reddish pink, in a lab sample.

item.title: Cameron Hamilton Poised to Lead FEMA Once More
item.description: Cameron Hamilton defended the agency last year when President Trump talked about eliminating it. Emergency managers hope for more stability if he’s confirmed as administrator.
item.dc:creator: Scott Dance
item.media:description: Just over a year after being fired, Cameron Hamilton is on the brink of assuming the helm of FEMA once again.
